newsitem.title: USA: N.J. groups say support $2.8 bln pension deal.
newsitem.headline: N.J. groups say support $2.8 bln pension deal.

text.p: Several interest groups got behind Gov. Whitman's plan to sell $2.8 billion of pension bonds Monday, though neither chamber of the New Jersey Legislature was ready this week to vote on the matter.

At a State House press conference, the state School Boards Association, the League of Municipalities and an ad hoc group of social service organizations urged lawmakers to enact the plan, which has stalled amid opposition in the State House.
Treasurer Brian Clymer appeared with several county and local officials who said the refinancing plan made sense to them, and added that it would provide them property tax relief.

Clymer said a key component of the the plan would update the valuation of the investment portfolio to recognize gains in the recent bull market, and allow localities to defer commensurate levels of pension contributions until July 1, 1998. The aggregate saving to local government would be $107 million.

The state is hoping the Legislature will allow it to use the same strategy to avoid paying $590 million in the budget year starting July 1. The plan involves selling $2.8 billion of bonds to finance the state's unfunded pension obligations.
Clymer said the components providing savings to the state and to local governments were two parts of a package deal.
"I don't think we'll see this split out," he said at the press conference. "They're presented as one package."

Whitman also defended the dividend for her budget. "I think today's taxpayers should be allowed to benefit," she said, noting that future taxpayers will pay less in debt service than they would in pension contributions.
